verdicts.lens: Art direction — composition, staging, materials, lighting, render quality, typography and information design. Benchmarks reconstructed from memory (I have not opened any reference on disk): Wilson Sasha/Alexia studio renders, McIntosh MC275/MC1.25KW press shots, Devialet Expert Pro product images.
verdicts.verdict: Forced verdict on all twelve: none of these would be mistaken for the photograph. Not one. Mean moved from ~42 to ~42 — the core repairs (front-hemisphere light, planar floor, contact shadows, pinned readouts) bought real ground, and the twelve unverified stage edits gave most of it back. Amp is the one genuine win (+13: the monoblock is finally the hero, framed, with modelled fins and feet). Streamer is the worst regression (−7: its diagram card now renders as 85% dead black — both Graph plots and 34 of 36 ribbon cells simply do not draw, while the DOM labels on the same card update live, so the geometry is broken, not the update loop). Turntable and DAC also went backwards, both by letting the card grow and the hero shrink. Physics is in far better shape than the pictures: RIAA at 3180/318/75 µs with poles at 50.05/2122 Hz, LR4 at −6.02 dB per leg summing to −0.015 dB, sealed at −12 dB/oct, 1 Pa rms → 94 dB → ξ = 0.546 µm peak, Schroeder from Sabine — a measurement editor would sign most of this off. An art director would not let a single frame run. Now the direct question. The single biggest remaining thing is not the diagram cards, though they are the biggest composition problem: it is that nothing in this piece has a specular layer sitting in front of what is underneath it. Every bright thing is either a clipped 100%-white line — the shelf trims, the rack posts, the plinth chamfers, the tonearm, the platter strobe, the sub's surround ring, all pinned at pure white with a bloom halo — or a flat emissive patch with nothing over it: the McIntosh meter is a light-blue decal with zero environment reflection across its lens, the displays are stickers, the record is dead matte with no groove sheen, the cabinets are one flat value with no clearcoat ramp down the side, and the cards are matte black rectangles with no sheen at all. The histogram is bimodal — clipped whites and 2%-luminance blacks — and a real product render lives in the long grey ramp between them, the wrapped highlight that rolls from white through mid-grey into the body colour and tells you the surface continues. Fix the specular layer and the same geometry jumps twenty points across all twelve stages. The proximate cause is two emitters in core/env.js: a 0.85 m-tall strip at intensity 11.0 and a 0.7 m-tall strip at 12.0, narrow enough that every alloy edge in the set returns a hard clipped line instead of a gradient.

scores.note: +13, the only real gain. Monoblock is now the hero, framed, fins and feet modelled. Held down by the meter reading as a decal and a flat 2D schematic slab.
−1. Real floor reflection is a genuine gain; given back by a clipped off-screen label, an orange plinth strip, cartoon cable swooshes and 25% dead sky.
−6. Deck shrank, foreground blob intrudes, six labels pile up top-left over two near-empty cards. Record still dead matte.
−7. Seven plot regions on one card against an addendum limit of three; card crosses the top frame edge and the rail.
−8. Card content does not render. Best label system in the piece, attached to a black void.
+4. Card moved clear of the hero, rack whole in frame. Worst shelf-neon in the set.
+2. Teal seam gone, sub bigger and better modelled, mode map legible. New light-leak blob; rack blown white.
+4. Rack reads as one object, RIAA plot correct. Still no identifiable hero.
+3. Plot is correct and clean, but it is a frontal poster and the hardware is cropped by the frame bottom.
−1. Framing repaired by the lead; drivers are still holes and the cabinet is still one flat value.
−2. Hero conditioner still entirely behind a black slab. Orange bars are the loudest thing in frame.
+2. Bloom fog reduced. Still the busiest frame, with traces drawing in front of solid geometry.

verdicts.lens: Measurement editor / loudspeaker engineer — every on-screen number recomputed from the stated inputs, every animation checked against the three hard bans, every graph checked for readability as a measurement.
verdicts.verdict: The arithmetic has improved enormously since round 1 and most of it now survives an independent recomputation: I re-derived RIAA (50.05 / 500.49 / 2122.07 Hz, record + playback = 0.000 dB), LR4 (−6.021 dB at each fc, three-way cascade sum −0.015 dB worst case at 105 Hz, 660° of rotation in band, group-delay peak 6.93 ms at 54 Hz, LR2-all-positive nulling to −28.8 / −57.6 dB), the sealed-box algebra (α 3.732, fc 60.91 Hz, Qtc 0.742, f3 58.2 Hz, and it is correctly called second order), excursion ∝ 1/f² (7.575 → 0.682 mm, ratio 11.1 = (100/30)²), Small's efficiency and the 91.4 dB sensitivity, 6.02N+1.76, ZOH −3.9224 dB at fs/2, noise-shaping at order 2 / OSR 64, jitter SNR, Hertzian contact (a = 3.03 µm, 482 MPa mean, 723 MPa peak), Baerwald nulls and 17.32 mm overhang, room modes and Schroeder at 105 Hz, p/(ρc) and ξ = u/ω, the middle-ear 27 dB against a 29.6 dB mismatch, and class-AB peak dissipation (150.5 W total, 25 W per device, at 38.9 % of maximum output). Almost every one checks. But yes — there is material a measurement editor would refuse to print. Four things in particular. (1) The DAC compares a measured 67.4 dB in-band SNR taken at roughly −9.9 dBFS against an 85.2 dB model defined for a full-scale sine, and attributes the whole 18 dB gap to "white-noise assumptions" when about half of it is simply input level; that is a rigged comparison. (2) The air chapter draws air parcels moving at 0.754 × the drawn wave speed — the code deliberately maximises ξ·k — on the one page whose entire thesis is that air does not travel, while the caption says c/û = 100 000. (3) The piece contradicts itself across chapters on the same hardware: the voice coil is 6.2 Ω in `speaker`/`air` and 5.4 Ω in `amp`/`xover`; the loudspeaker is 91.4 dB/2.83 V in two chapters and 89 dB in the overview; the cartridge is 285 µV rms in `turntable` and 300 µV rms in `phono`/`overview`; the phono stage is 64 dB in its own chapter and 60 dB in the overview; and the headline mains draw of 2282 W is computed from "two 600 W monoblocks" into 4 Ω when every other chapter says the load is 8 Ω and the amplifier is 300 W. (4) Only `xover` carries numerals on its axes; the RIAA plot, the preamp S/N plot, the sealed-response and excursion plots, and the DAC's six plots cannot be read to a value, and the subwoofer's pressure map has no colour key at all. Visually the piece is not yet close to a product render: `streamer` and `turntable` ship overlay cards that are essentially blank, the DAC card ghosts the rack through it, `power` puts a full-frame diagram over a hero that is a footnote at the bottom of the shot, `overview` prints a label at x = −167 px, and every rack stage frames the whole rack rather than its own 92–160 mm chassis. Fix the three hard-ban and cross-stage contradictions first — they are what a reader can catch you on — then the blank cards and the framing.

findings.what: src/core/env.js: `frontStrip` (18 × 0.85 m at intensity 11.0, line 115) and `strip` (17 × 0.7 m at 12.0, line 136) are narrow enough that every alloy edge in the set returns a clipped 100%-white line rather than a highlight with a rolloff. Count them in one frame: preamp has ~12 blown shelf-lip bars plus four full-length blown rack posts; turntable has a blown plinth chamfer and a blown tonearm; sub has a blown surround ring; the rack in sub and preamp is a neon wireframe. This single pair of emitters is why the piece reads as CGI.
findings.fix: Widen and dim both: frontStrip to 18 × 2.6 m at ~3.4, strip to 17 × 2.2 m at ~3.8. Keep the same positions and rotations. The reflected image of the source then spans enough of each fillet to produce a gradient instead of a clipped line. Re-shoot preamp and phono to confirm the shelf trims read as a bright-to-mid ramp, not a bar. If the scene then reads flat, raise `beauty` (line 108) from 4.6 to ~6.0 rather than putting the strips back.

findings.what: src/stages/streamer.js: the overlay card is ~85% dead black. Neither DIAG.Graph draws at its declared size — only a ~50 px-wide fragment of one frame plus a sliver of the amber jitter band appears at the card's far right edge (around x 2900–3000, y 1450–1750 in shots/streamer.png), against a declared GW 0.235 × GH 0.155 that should be ~440 px wide. The AES3 ribbon shows 2 of its 36 Swarm cells. The DOM labels on the same card update live (106 ms, Δt = −38 ps, 0x5A9DF7), so update() runs; the failure is geometric. This is the worst functional defect in the set.
findings.fix: Debug the overlay build in buildOverlay() (lines 387–470). Check that og/eg are not being scaled or re-parented after `og.position.set(OGX, GY, 0.0006)`, that Graph's internal frame uses the w/h passed rather than a stale value, and that the Swarm `.update(i => …)` callback returns a position for every i in 0..7 and 0..27 rather than falling through to undefined for most indices. Re-shoot and confirm both plot boxes fill their declared width before touching anything else in this stage.

findings.what: src/stages/amp.js line ~575: the meter's additive specular layer contributes nothing. `specMat` is roughness 0.02 / envMapIntensity 2.6 on a curvedPlane with sag 0.0004 m — 0.4 mm across a ~100 mm lens, effectively flat. At mirror roughness on a flat plane the reflection vector at this camera angle lands on the dark shell, so the environment returns ~zero and the meter reads exactly as the brief's failure case: a glowing decal with no glass in front of it. This same object appears in overview, preamp, dac, phono, sub and air, so it is six frames, not one.
findings.fix: Raise the sag from 0.0004 to ~0.005 m and roughness from 0.02 to ~0.055. The convex lens then sweeps the frontStrip across the glass as a soft diagonal band, and at 0.055 the band has a width instead of being a needle that misses. Separately, drop the dial gradient in dialTexture() (line ~318) by about 40% — take the stops to #3a90c0 / #24699c / #114b78 / #0a3459 — so the glass highlight can clip above the face. The reflection must be the brightest thing in the meter window, not the dial.

findings.what: src/stages/speaker.js: the bass drivers have no cone. Crop shots/speaker.png at (1050,1050) 1000×900: each driver is a glossy black trim ring around a completely flat dark disc — no surround roll, no dust cap or phase plug, no spider, no basket spokes, no mounting screws. It reads as a hole. On the stage titled Motor & Cabinet, with a Wilson render as the benchmark, this is fatal; the driver is 60% of what a reader looks at. The same drivers appear in overview and air.
findings.fix: Build the driver properly with GEO helpers: a half-torus surround (mats().rubber, ~8 mm roll), a lathed cone from the surround inner edge to the neck (mats().cone or coneWeave), a domed dust cap (mats().dome), six countersunk GEO.screw on the flange, and a visible cast basket arm between flange and neck. The surround roll is what catches the front strip and makes a driver read as a driver — without it no amount of lighting will save the frame.

findings.what: src/stages/turntable.js: the record is dead matte with no groove sheen, despite vinylMats() (line 367) doing the right things — anisotropy 0.85 on a lathe, clearcoat 0.85, grooveRoughTex with 770 bands. The map is collapsing in the mip chain: 770 bands across a ~300 px disc radius is ~2.5 px per band, so with anisotropy 8 and mipmapping the whole surface averages to one uniform roughness. Meanwhile the platter strobe ring beside it is blown to pure white. The priority is exactly inverted: the record is the subject and it is the only matte thing in frame.
findings.fix: Stop trying to resolve individual grooves. In grooveRoughTex(), set `t.generateMipmaps = false; t.minFilter = THREE.LinearFilter;` and drive the sheen from a band count a camera actually resolves — pass ~90 rather than 770 — so the concentric roughness variation survives to screen. Add the features a photograph really shows: a smooth lead-in land at R_OUT, a lead-out land and 4–6 inter-track gaps as distinctly smoother rings. Then dull the strobe ring (rimMat.roughness 0.34 → 0.5) so the record wins the specular contest.

findings.what: src/app.css line 51: `.wlab` is `white-space:nowrap; max-width:36ch` with no overflow rule, and `.wlab .k` (line 66) inherits nowrap. Any kicker longer than 36 characters spills outside its own scrim onto the render. Visible in air ('FLOOR BOUNCE · SOURCE 0.985 M BELOW THE FLOOR' — 'THE FLOOR' prints over the rack chassis with no backing), power ('THE FIRST TWO AT TRUE ×26 · THE THIRD THAT SAME SWING ~3000 MORE' overprints the neighbouring label), and turntable ('45/45 GROOVE — 1800 : 1 · MOTION 1 : 1000' runs under the adjacent card).
findings.fix: In src/app.css: remove `max-width:36ch` from `.wlab` and add `white-space:normal; max-width:34ch` to `.wlab .k`. Long kickers then wrap to a second line inside the scrim and the box grows to fit. Keep `white-space:nowrap` on `.wlab .v` only, so values never break.

findings.what: Every one of the twelve panels ends mid-sentence under the `#panel-scroll.more` fade mask (src/app.css line 120). Xover loses its entire 'COMMONLY GOT WRONG' block — only the red title survives; sub loses the last line of its mode arithmetic; amp, speaker, air, streamer, phono, preamp, overview and dac all cut mid-word. In a still frame a fade that truncates mid-glyph reads as a crop, not as a scroll affordance. Twelve of twelve stages also exceed the 320-word ceiling in ADDENDUM C.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) In app.css move the mask start from `calc(100% - 34px)` to `calc(100% - 56px)` and add a visible affordance — a hairline rule plus a small chevron — so a reader sees 'there is more' rather than 'this is broken'. (2) Instruct every stage to cut content() to what fits above the fold at 1600×1000, roughly 230 words at 13.5 px/1.66, and to place .key or .myth in the first third per ADDENDUM C. Xover and sub are the urgent two: their callouts are entirely invisible.

findings.what: src/stages/power.js: the hero conditioner is still completely hidden. The diagram card covers roughly 55% of the safe box and sits directly in front of bay 0; the only visible hardware is the chassis below it and a chopped display unit cut off by the top frame edge. Round 1 raised exactly this and it was not fixed. The three copper-orange bars are also the loudest element in frame and orange is a fourth hue — CONTRACT §3.5 permits cyan, amber, red and green only.
findings.fix: Move the card to camera-right and shrink it: card centre to roughly [0.62, 0.52, −2.70] at 0.34 × 0.26, so it sits beside bay 0 rather than over it, and re-target the shot on the conditioner. Recolour the three conductor bars from the orange fill to PAL.am at ~0.30 opacity with a PAL.am hairline edge — the bars should read as a diagram band, not as the brightest object in the render.

findings.what: src/stages/dac.js: seven DIAG.Graph instances on one card. ADDENDUM B caps this at two cards and three plot regions. The card also crosses the top frame edge (clipped at y=0) and extends left across the chapter rail past the x<160 safe-box limit, so the rail's inactive items become unreadable, and its lower edge covers the DAC chassis that is the subject.
findings.fix: Keep three plots and move the rest into content(): retain the sinc-sum reconstruction, the ZOH-and-its-removal pair, and the shaped-noise FFT. Delete the aperture/images plot, the Δ-Σ bit stream, the amplitude-floor plot and the 20 kHz-sampled plot from the scene — the last is a duplicate of the first idea. Shrink the card to fit inside x 160…1120, y 90…930 at 1600×1000 and raise its lower edge clear of the hero chassis.

findings.what: The chapter rail is illegible in half the stages. Its inactive items are var(--ink-3) grey on the raw canvas, so they vanish against a matte black diagram card (power, dac, sub, preamp, air) and again against a blown-white rack shelf (sub). In power, ten of twelve rail rows are effectively unreadable.
findings.fix: In src/app.css give the rail its own scrim independent of what is behind it — on the `#rail` container add `background:linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(7,8,11,.72) 0,rgba(7,8,11,.55) 62%,transparent 100%)` with a 4 px backdrop blur — and lift the inactive `.chap .t` colour from var(--ink-3) to var(--ink-2) at 0.62 alpha. The rail is chrome; it must never depend on the render behind it.

findings.what: src/core/reflector.js: the planar floor reflection is incomplete and inconsistent. In overview the speakers' drivers reflect but the cabinets do not, leaving floating dark rings on a grey field; in speaker the cabinet is absent from its own reflection while unrelated pale rectangles appear; in air the rack reflects as disconnected pale fragments rather than a coherent mirror image. The result reads as smudge, and a broken reflection is worse than none — it is the first thing a retoucher would flag.
findings.fix: Check the reflector's camera layers/frustum and its near/far planes: the missing objects are the tall ones, which suggests the mirror camera's frustum or its clip plane is cutting geometry above a height. Also confirm every stage's hardware is on the layer the reflector renders. Then bring the blur down — the current radius destroys the silhouette; a product-floor reflection wants a sharp first 200 mm falling to blur over ~600 mm, not uniform mush.

findings.what: src/core/room.js ttPlinth() line ~160: the `under` slab uses mats().wood and, lit by the current rig, renders as a saturated bright-orange strip along the plinth's front edge. It is the most saturated element in both the overview and speaker frames and is a hue outside the permitted palette. It reads as an accident, not as a material.
findings.fix: Either darken and desaturate it — clone mats().wood with `color.setHex(0x1a1410)` and `roughness 0.7` — or replace it with mats().anodBlack. Nothing in this set should carry a warm saturated hue except PAL.am used deliberately as a diagram accent.

findings.what: src/stages/air.js: the cyan wavefront traces draw in front of solid geometry. In shots/air.png the long trace running from upper-left crosses the rack chassis and the right monoblock and prints over them rather than being occluded; the amber floor-bounce rays print over the sofa and over the parcel card. Traces that ignore depth are the classic overlay-demo tell and they destroy the illusion that the diagram lives in the room.
findings.fix: Ensure every DIAG.Trace in this stage is created with default depthTest (do not pass `depthTest:false`) and that renderOrder is not being forced above the opaque pass. Where a trace legitimately needs to be seen through hardware, split it: draw the occluded segment at 0.2 opacity with depthTest on, not the whole line on top of everything.

findings.what: src/stages/air.js: the frame is flat and hazed. A broad grey wash covers the middle band with a straight horizontal top edge around y≈860 in shots/air.png; below it, contrast collapses and the floor becomes a featureless blue-grey slab. Combined with eleven labels, six floating wavefront ellipses and a sofa that is an untextured grey wedge, the closing spread has no focal point at all.
findings.fix: Kill the wash (or give it a soft vertical falloff so there is no seam) and cut to one idea: the direct ray plus the single floor bounce, with the parcel-displacement card. Delete the concentric wavefront ellipses — they are perfect uniform-width circles with no falloff and read as vector art. Then reframe: the current fill is roughly 0.30 with dead space above and below; take it to ~0.45 on the listening position.

findings.what: src/stages/xover.js: the graph card is a flat, perfectly frontal black rectangle occupying the whole upper half — no perspective, no material, no thickness, hard corners. It is a screenshot pasted into a photograph. Meanwhile the hardware is pushed to the bottom third and the lower chassis is cut off by the frame edge, and the entire left 15% of the frame is empty grey.
findings.fix: Rotate the card 12–15° toward the camera axis so it sits in the room rather than on the lens, shrink it to ~0.62 of its current size, and move it camera-right. Raise the shot's target and lower fill so the crossover chassis and the unit below it are complete in frame. Give the card a 3 mm bevelled edge with mats().anodBlack so it has a lit rim — a card with a modelled edge stops reading as a compositing layer.

findings.what: src/stages/phono.js: there is no identifiable hero. Six near-identical chassis fill the rack and nothing marks which one is the phono stage — same value, same lighting, same detail level. The 'MOVING-COIL PHONO STAGE · 100 Ω' label floats without a leader to any specific bay. Round 1 raised 'no identifiable hero' and it is unchanged.
findings.fix: Isolate the subject the way a product photographer would: add a soft negative-fill card in front of bays 0,1,2,4,5 (a dark plane in the overlay at ~0.35 opacity) so the phono bay is the only fully lit chassis, and add a `cls:'lead'` label with a visible leader dot anchored to that bay's fascia. Alternatively re-frame tighter on bay 3 at fill ~0.55 so the neighbouring bays are cropped.

findings.what: src/stages/turntable.js: six label cards pile into the upper-left quadrant and collide. '45/45 GROOVE' runs its third line under 'MOVING COIL' and the value truncates mid-number at 'pitch 12'; 'W — VERTICAL' and 'U — LATERAL' overlap the groove card beneath them. Behind them the two diagram cards are nearly empty — the left is a near-uniform blue-grey rectangle with a small stylus glyph in one corner, the right a few thin schematic lines on black. Three cards, against a limit of two, and none of them is carrying its area.
findings.fix: Cut to one card. Keep the 45/45 groove cross-section with the stylus in it and fill the card — the tip radii, the wall angles and the modulation are the picture. Delete the generator schematic card entirely and put e = Bl·v̇ in content(). Drop to three labels: groove geometry, tip velocity, coil output. Then raise the deck's fill from ~0.34 to ~0.50 and re-target on the platter centre.

findings.what: src/stages/amp.js: the circuit card is 2D linework — yellow capacitor symbols and white/cyan wires on matte black, a textbook schematic floating in a photographic set. Its right edge slices through the rack behind it and the rack's chassis shows through inconsistently at the boundary. The genuinely good content on that card, the twin-rail drift animation with the 7.8 × 10¹¹ field-to-carrier ratio, is a 20 px strip at the very bottom edge.
findings.fix: Invert the card: make the two-rail drift comparison the whole card at 3× its current size — that is the one physical idea a picture tells better than prose here, and it is the contract's headline demand. Move the schematic into content() as an .eq or delete it. Then pull the card clear of the rack silhouette (camera-right, in front of the backdrop, not in front of the rack).

findings.what: src/stages/sub.js: an unmotivated white glow blob sits at roughly (1000,2240) in shots/sub.png — a soft hard-centred flare with no source, in front of the rack's lower shelves. The rack itself is blown to white behind the mode card. Together they make the left half of the frame read as a light leak.
findings.fix: Find and remove the emissive or DIAG.glow sprite at that world position (bottom-front of the rack). If it is meant to mark the sub's mains feed, replace it with a small LED at the correct scale rather than a 120 px flare. Then either move the mode card so it is not competing with the rack, or reduce the rack's exposure locally once the env.js strip fix lands.

findings.what: src/stages/overview.js: a label is clipped off the left edge of the frame — a dark rounded fragment with the letters 'er' visible at x≈0, y≈600 in the 1600-wide view, sitting on the chapter rail. Its anchor projects outside the viewport and the collision handler is not dropping it.
findings.fix: Give that label `priority: 0` so it is dropped on collision, or move its anchor inboard of x=160. Then audit the whole stage against the safe box: nothing may cross x<160 or x>1120 at 1600×1000.

findings.what: src/stages/overview.js: the signal path reads as vector art, not as anything physical. The cyan cable arcs are uniform-radius glowing tubes that arc over the components and plug into nothing at either end; the mains loop swoops across the floor in a clean sine; and there are three disconnected dashed cyan segments floating in mid-air with no anchor (visible at roughly x 250, 900 and 1100 in the 1600-wide view).
findings.fix: Terminate every path at a real connector — GEO.rcaJack / GEO.xlr / GEO.bindingPost on the chassis it leaves and the one it enters — and route it with cable sag rather than an arc. Delete the free-floating dashed fragments or connect them into a continuous run. A path that starts and ends in mid-air is the reason this reads as a diagram of a hi-fi rather than a photograph of one.

findings.what: src/stages/speaker.js: the cabinet has no clearcoat. Crop shots/speaker.png at (1050,1050): the side panel and the baffle sit at the same flat mid-grey with no vertical gradient, no environment reflection and no long unbroken highlight running down the cabinet. The brief names this specific quality; it is absent. The baffle corner is a hard edge with a token bevel and no wrapped highlight, so the cabinet does not read as one solid.
findings.fix: Use mats().pianoBlack (clearcoat 1.0 / clearcoatRoughness 0.028) or a clone of it rather than the current flat material, and increase the front and side edge radii to ~6 mm so a continuous fillet highlight runs the full height of the cabinet. That single unbroken vertical is what makes a Wilson render read as lacquer over a dark base.

findings.what: src/stages/speaker.js: three overlay regions are visible at once (motor cutaway card, Thiele–Small card, excursion inset) against the two-card limit, and two of them bisect the hero's silhouette. The T-S plot has no y-axis annotation at all and its cyan trace runs off the left edge of the plot box and terminates on the boundary rather than being framed. The amber fill in the excursion plot is a rectangle with a hard vertical right edge that has no relation to the curve running through it, and it is half hidden behind the EXCURSION label.
findings.fix: Drop to two cards and move both clear of the cabinet silhouette (camera-right). Label the T-S y-axis in dB with gridline values and set the x-range so the trace is fully inside the box. Either make the amber region a real area under the curve or label it explicitly as the Xmax band with its dB/mm value; as drawn it is unreadable.

findings.what: src/stages/amp.js: the heatsink fin stack is a single dark mass. The geometry is there and it is good, but no fin tip carries a highlight, so the sink reads as a black comb rather than as machined alloy. On the McIntosh reference every fin tip carries a specular line and that is most of what sells the object's scale.
findings.fix: Once the env.js strips are widened, add a narrow raking source specifically for the fin tips — or, within the stage, give the fin material a lower roughness on the tip band. Simplest: chamfer the fin tips by ~0.4 mm using bevelBox rather than a square end, so each tip has a facet that can return the front strip.

findings.what: src/stages/amp.js: the meter dial layout is wrong. In the crop the scale arc occupies only the upper-left of the window with a large dead blue area at the right; the needle pivot sits low and left of centre with a crude grey rectangle at its base; and the numerals collide — '100' and '300' overlap each other and the needle covers '300'. A McIntosh meter's arc is centred with the pivot below the window's lower edge.
findings.fix: In dialTexture() recentre the arc on W/2 and move the pivot below the drawn area (pivot y ≈ H × 1.18) so the arc sweeps symmetrically across the full window width. Increase numeral spacing so no two labels are within 1.4 × glyph width, and replace the pivot rectangle with a small turned boss.

findings.what: src/stages/preamp.js: the card is half empty and one of its captions is invisible. The lower plot region carries a single thin dashed line across mostly blank black, and the caption 'LADDER AFTER THE GAIN BLOCK' is drawn in dark grey directly on the dark plot with no scrim — it is effectively unreadable at 100%. The 'LINE PREAMP · FIXED GAIN, THEN THE LADDER' label is also half-greyed by an occlusion band that cuts through its own glyphs.
findings.fix: Give the in-plot caption a scrim (drop `cls:'plain'`) or move it above the plot box like the other captions in this stage. Fill or shrink the lower plot region — a plot that is 80% empty should be a smaller plot. For the LINE PREAMP label, set `occlude:false` since it is annotating a card, not a world point.

findings.what: src/stages/phono.js: the RIAA plot's background is split — the right half of the plot box carries a warm brown/maroon grid tint, the left half does not, with a hard vertical boundary and no legend explaining it. It reads as a rendering fault rather than as a band.
findings.fix: Either remove the tint or make it a labelled DIAG.addBand with a caption stating what it marks (e.g. 'above 2122 Hz — the 75 µs pole'). An unexplained coloured region on a measurement plot is the fastest way to lose a measurement editor.

findings.what: src/stages/sub.js: the mode map has no colour key. Orange and cyan lobes carry no legend for pressure sign or magnitude, the 'Ψ = 0' nodal-line label is tiny and overprinted by 'the sofa sits on the centre line', and the orange is a hue outside the permitted palette. The map is the best piece of information design in the piece and it is unreadable as a measurement.
findings.fix: Add a two-swatch key ('+p' / '−p') with the peak value in Pa, in the card's lower-left. Move the Ψ = 0 label clear of the sofa caption. Recolour the positive lobes from orange to PAL.am so the frame holds to cyan/amber.

findings.what: src/stages/xover.js: the plots are under-annotated for a measurement audience. The magnitude plot labels only '20 Hz' and '20 kHz' at the extremes with no decade ticks, the group-delay panel below has no y-axis values at all, and the dashed orange traces (the LR2-with-all-drivers-positive case) appear in no legend — the reader has to infer them from a floating caption.
findings.fix: Label decades at 20/100/1k/10k/20k on the magnitude x-axis and 0/2/4/6/8 ms on the group-delay y-axis. Add a two-line legend inside the plot box naming the solid cyan (LR4 sections), the pale sum trace and the dashed case. Recolour the dashed traces from orange to PAL.am.

findings.what: src/app.css .wlab: the label scrims read as operating-system notification toasts, not as editorial annotation — 60% black fill, 4 px backdrop blur, 4 px radius, a white 1 px ring and a 10 px drop shadow. In a magazine a callout over a photograph is a hairline leader plus set text, or a clean flat rule-bounded box. The current treatment is the single most 'web app' element in every frame.
findings.fix: Flatten it: drop the box-shadow, drop the border-radius to 2 px, drop the white ring to rgba(255,255,255,.03), and raise the fill to rgba(7,8,11,.74) so the type carries on contrast rather than on blur. Add the leader dot (.wlab.lead already exists) to every label that annotates a world point, and use cls:'plain' wherever the label sits over dead space.

findings.what: src/stages/air.js: the sofa is the largest foreground object and it is an untextured low-poly grey wedge with no cushions, no seams and no upholstery material. It also reappears clipped at the bottom-left of overview. A finished set piece is cheap here and an unfinished one is expensive — it is the object closest to camera in the closing frame.
findings.fix: Either apply mats().cloth with a visible weave and split the mass into base, back and two cushions with 20 mm fillets and a stitch line, or crop it out of both frames entirely. A grey wedge is worse than no sofa.

findings.what: src/stages/turntable.js: the tonearm is blown to pure white along its whole length — armtube, bearing yoke and headshell all clip, so the arm has no form and the cartridge and stylus are unreadable at the groove. On a stage about a diamond reading a wall, the diamond is invisible.
findings.fix: Reduce the arm material's envMapIntensity and raise its roughness (a real armwand is satin, not mirror), and give the headshell and cartridge body a darker material so they separate from the arm. This will largely resolve itself once the env.js strips are widened, but check it explicitly after that change.

findings.what: src/stages/turntable.js: a large unidentifiable dark object with a bright ring intrudes across the left 20% of the frame, crossing the x<160 safe-box limit. It reads as a black blob competing with the hero for attention and cannot be recognised as a loudspeaker driver at that crop.
findings.fix: Adjust the shot azimuth by ~8° or raise fill so that object falls outside the frame. If it must stay, push it into shadow — a foreground element that is neither identifiable nor readable is subtracting from the frame.

findings.what: src/stages/overview.js: the composition is under-filled. The system occupies roughly the middle third of the frame with ~25% dead near-black above and a large empty foreground below, and the label cards cluster in one horizontal band across the middle rather than distributing. The sofa fragment clips awkwardly at bottom-left.
findings.fix: Raise fill from its current ~0.35 to ~0.46 and lower the camera from its current dollhouse height so the speakers reach nearer the top of the safe box. Distribute the five labels — two high-left, one high-right, two low — instead of a single band, and either include the sofa properly or move the camera so it falls outside frame.

findings.what: src/stages/amp.js and src/stages/sub.js: the contract requires both monoblocks (LAYOUT.monoL/monoR) and both subs (LAYOUT.subL/R) to be visible in their own stage. In shots/amp.png only one monoblock is in frame; in shots/sub.png only one sub. The pair is part of what the stage is claiming.
findings.fix: Widen or re-azimuth each shot to include the second unit, even partially and defocused at the frame edge — a single unit on a stage titled 'Monoblocks' (plural) is a factual mismatch with the chapter rail label.

findings.what: src/stages/power.js: the top display unit is cut off by the top frame edge, and a hard white specular blob with no defined shape sits on the conditioner's front-left face at roughly (940,1400) in shots/power.png. Neither is a highlight — the blob has no form and reads as a light leak.
findings.fix: Lower the shot target so the unit above is either fully in frame or fully out; a chassis clipped by the frame edge with a visible partial fascia is the worst of both. Trace the blob to whichever emissive or spot is landing there and either shape it or remove it.

findings.what: src/stages/air.js:172 sets XI_K = 0.754, so the parcel window draws each air parcel oscillating with peak velocity 0.754 × the drawn wave speed. The crest marker (update(), line ~418) advances at exactly ω/k = c on the same clock, so the reader watches air moving at three-quarters the speed of sound on the very page whose thesis is 'air is not a conveyor'. The panel simultaneously prints c/û = 100×10³. The label only discloses the SPATIAL magnification (×75,400); it never states that the as-drawn velocity ratio is 1.33 : 1 instead of 10⁵ : 1.
findings.fix: Do what power.js already does. Add the as-drawn ratio to the AIR PARCELS label and to content(): 'as drawn only ×1.3 faster than the parcels, truly ×1.00×10⁵'. Better: drop XI_K to ~0.25 (still a visible ±25 % density swing, ξ·k monotonic with a large margin), recompute MAG from it, and add a second marker that runs at the drawn wave speed so the contrast is visible rather than asserted.

findings.what: The overlay card in shots/streamer.png is an empty black plate (device x 725–1355, y 285–705 at 2000-px width) carrying three captions and nothing else. The AES3 subframe bit stream, the buffer strip chart and the clock eye are all absent from the plate; the only geometry visible is a fragment clipped against the card's right edge at x 1275–1310. The three labels therefore point at blank card.
findings.fix: In src/stages/streamer.js, re-check the card-local origin and scale of the three regions against the plate rectangle — the content appears to be positioned near or past the plate's right edge. Verify with node verify.mjs streamer and read the PNG before declaring done.

findings.what: Both overlay cards render as near-empty navy rectangles (shots/turntable.png, x 340–700 and 780–1100, y 210–520). The 45/45 groove cross-section at 1800:1 — the subject of the chapter, and what the 'u — lateral' / 'w — vertical' labels annotate — is reduced to one small circle at about (515,300). The generator card shows a coil ~12 px across. Four labels annotate drawings the reader cannot see.
findings.fix: In src/stages/turntable.js, buildGrooveCard/buildGeneratorCard: the drawn extent is a small fraction of the card plate. Rescale the groove section so the 60 µm groove at 1800:1 fills most of its card, or shrink the plates to fit the drawings. Re-shoot and look.

findings.what: content() and the SHAPED NOISE label print 'in-band 67.4 dB · model 85.2 dB' and explain the gap as 'white-noise assumptions flatter a one-bit quantiser'. The model, DSP.noiseShapedSnrDb(1, 2, 64), is defined for a FULL-SCALE sine. The measured figure comes from a three-tone signal at MOD_GAIN = 0.5 whose rms is 0.2264 against a full-scale sine's 0.7071 — i.e. the input is 9.9 dB below full scale. About 10 dB of the 17.8 dB 'gap' is just input level. The stated conclusion is therefore not supported by the measurement.
findings.fix: In src/stages/dac.js analyseStream(), report dynamic range referred to full scale: SPEC.snrMeas + 20·log10(0.7071/rms_of_input) — or re-run the modulator at an input whose rms equals a full-scale sine and quote that. Then restate the residual gap (which will be ~8 dB, not 18) and keep the sentence about idle tones / white-noise assumptions honest to that number.

findings.what: The same hardware carries different primaries in different chapters. (a) Voice-coil dc resistance: speaker.js TS.Re = 6.2 Ω and air.js TS.Re = 6.2 Ω, but amp.js RE_COIL = 5.4 Ω (line 60) and xover.js RE_COIL = 5.4 Ω (line 58) — and both use it for the damping-resistance argument. (b) Sensitivity: speaker.js and air.js both derive 91.38 dB @ 2.83 V/1 m; overview.js:45 asserts SENS = 89, and its 89.5 dB / 75.8 dB SPL figures follow from the wrong number. (c) Cartridge output: turntable.js derives E_RMS = 285 µV at 5 cm/s; phono.js V_CART = 0.30 mV and overview.js V_CART = 0.30 mV. (d) Phono gain: phono.js G_STAGE_DB = 64.0; overview.js G_PHONO = 60.0. (e) Amplifier: amp.js is 300 W into 8 Ω and every load in the piece is 8 Ω nominal, but power.js:25 and overview.js:50 compute the headline 2281.8 W / 9.92 A mains draw from 'two 600 W monoblocks' (the 4 Ω rating). At 8 Ω the true full-output draw is (2×300)/0.55 + 100 = 1191 W, 5.2 A rms — half the number the whole mains chapter is built on.
findings.fix: Pick one set and propagate. Suggested: Re = 6.2 Ω everywhere (update amp.js RE_COIL and xover.js RE_COIL, and recompute DAMP_PEN / RD_ACT / RD_PAS / RD_PCT); overview SENS = 91.4 (import or restate the derivation); overview G_PHONO = 64.0 and re-solve G_LADDER so the total still lands on an integer-dB ladder setting; cartridge 285 µV rms in all three; and in power.js/overview.js either state the operating point as '2 × 300 W into 8 Ω' and recompute P_SYS = 1191 W, I_RMS = 5.18 A, I_PK = 7.33 A (and every drift figure that follows), or say explicitly on screen that the mains figure is the 4 Ω worst case, not this system's load.

findings.what: Only xover.js adds DOM numerals to its plot axes. phono's RIAA graph (yRange −25…+25 dB, xRange 20–20 k), preamp's S/N graph (55…125 dB, 0…63), speaker's sealed-response (−27…+6 dB) and excursion (0…14 mm) graphs, sub's pressure map, air's comb plot and all six DAC plots carry tick marks with no values. Every one of these is presented as a measurement and none can be read to a value; the argument rests entirely on captions.
findings.fix: Copy the xover pattern (xover.js:508-531, the `tick()` helper with cls:'plain', occlude:false, priority:2) into phono (0, ±20 dB and 20 Hz / 20 kHz), preamp (60, 100, 120 dB and 0 / 63), speaker (0, −12, −24 dB; 0, 8, 14 mm; 15 Hz / 400 Hz and 24 / 200 Hz) and dac's two most load-bearing plots. Three to five short labels each; prune redundant captions to stay inside the ≲10-label budget.

findings.what: shots/dac.png: the diagram card is transparent to the hardware behind it. The rack's chrome posts (device x ≈ 650 and 1210) and its shelf edges (y ≈ 240, 437, 690) print straight through the plots, and the streamer/DAC fasciae bleed through around (900,530). This is the exact round-1 blocker ('rack shelves clearly visible through the graph plate'). The card also extends to device x ≈ 95, burying chapter-rail items 00–03, and two labels sit at y = 36 and 39, inside the masthead keep-out (y < 90).
findings.fix: In src/stages/dac.js: raise the card plate's opacity to 1.0 and make sure it writes depth AND that every rack mesh is depth-tested against it (the posts are being drawn with depthTest disabled or at a higher renderOrder). Shrink the card's world width by ~15 % and shift it right so its projected left edge clears x = 160. Move the RECONSTRUCTION and APERTURE labels below their plots (offset [0, +26]) so nothing lands above y = 90.

findings.what: Six plot regions on one card (reconstruction, ZOH, near-Nyquist, aperture/images, Δ-Σ bit stream, measured FFT) plus an amplitude-floor bar. ADDENDUM §B caps this at two cards and three plot regions. The result is unreadable at 1600×1000 and the DAC chassis itself is entirely hidden behind the card — the hardware chapter shows no hardware.
findings.fix: Keep three: the sinc reconstruction (the stage's one idea), the ZOH-as-intermediate, and the shaped-noise FFT. Move the near-Nyquist demonstration, the aperture/images plot and the amplitude-floor bar into content() as prose (the 2.205-points-per-cycle claim already survives as a sentence). Then reframe so the DAC chassis occupies at least a third of the safe-box height beside the card.

findings.what: shots/speaker.png: the motor cutaway card (device x 900–1400, y 160–620) renders as a washed-out pale blob. The back plate, pole piece, ring magnet, top plate and the 8.5 mm gap — the whole point of the section — are not distinguishable; the coil outline, the flux arrows and the spider are lost. The secLamp PointLight (intensity 2.4 at 1.5 m range) is over-lighting the section slabs to near-white against a black card.
findings.fix: In src/stages/speaker.js buildSection(): drop secLamp.intensity to ~0.8 and pull it further off-axis, and raise the hairline outline opacity (the OUT = 0x9aa3ae boxes, currently opacity 0.55) to ~0.9 with width 1.4. Then re-shoot and confirm the gap slot, the two coil sections and the flux path all read as separate parts.

findings.what: The 'LISTENING SEAT · 4.83 m from each loudspeaker · 14.1 ms of air' label is laid out at device x = −167 px — entirely off the left edge of the canvas. Only the two trailing characters ('er') are visible at x ≈ 0–20, y ≈ 730–780 in shots/overview.png. The label-collision system placed it rather than dropping it. 'SOURCE · TURNTABLE' also starts at x = 154, inside the chapter rail.
findings.fix: In src/stages/overview.js, move the listening-seat anchor to the chair's right side and give it offset [+90, 0] so its box lands inside x 160…1120; give SOURCE · TURNTABLE offset [+40, 0] or lower its priority so it is dropped rather than printed over the rail. Verify by reading back the .wlab.on bounding rects, not by eye.

findings.what: Composition is inverted. shot: frameShot([0.02, 0.40, −3.16], 0.30, {fill: 0.63}) aims 0.21 m above the conditioner (bay 0 centre ≈ 0.19 m) and frames a 0.30 m radius, so the RACK fills the frame. The cable card then occupies device x 180–1150, y 180–730 — the whole safe box — and the hero conditioner is a 170-px sliver at the bottom, partly under the transport bar. The card is also transparent: the streamer's OLED ('44.1 kHz 24 bit AES LOCK 128') and the monoblock heatsink read through it.
findings.fix: Retarget on the conditioner itself (y ≈ 0.19, its own bounding radius ~0.30) with fill 0.50, then truck the card to the right third at roughly half its present width — the same pattern amp.js uses successfully (amp.js:183-197). Raise the card plate opacity to 1.0 and give it depthWrite so nothing prints through.

findings.what: Every rack stage frames the whole rack instead of its own chassis, because `fill` is applied to a bounding RADIUS that is dominated by the chassis width (0.555 m) while `fill` is a fraction of the safe-box HEIGHT. phono.js uses HERO_R = 0.354 with fill 0.55: the 112 mm chassis ends up ~85 px tall in a 1250-px frame. Measured heights of the subject chassis in the current shots: phono ≈ 85 px, preamp ≈ 80 px, xover ≈ 145 px, streamer ≈ 80 px, dac hidden. In phono, preamp, streamer and xover a reader cannot tell which of the six identical rack units is the subject, and in phono and preamp the identifying label sits over a neighbouring unit's shelf.
findings.fix: For the six rack stages, pass frameShot a radius equal to the chassis HALF-HEIGHT plus a small margin (e.g. 0.09 for a 112 mm box) rather than its bounding sphere, and take fill 0.30–0.40 so the chassis is 250–340 px tall with the card beside it. Then anchor the identifying label to the subject chassis's own fascia with a short leader, not to the shelf above it.

findings.what: The pinned readouts and the world labels disagree in the same still frame on every animated stage, because the readouts refresh at 10 Hz while labels update every frame. Measured from the current shots: power reads CURRENT −6.31 A in the footer while the LIVE label on the same conductor says −11.75 A; air reads PARTICLE DISPL +0.265 µm while the parcel label says ξ = +0.544 of 0.546 µm peak (and the footer's +3.00 mm/s velocity is only consistent with its own 0.265, not with the label); sub reads CONE X −3.09 mm against a label of −3.37 mm; speaker reads COIL I −3.06 A against a label of −3.19 A. Since the piece is judged from stills, this reads as an arithmetic error.
findings.fix: Have update() write the SAME cached state object that readouts() reads, and drive the labels from that cached state rather than from the instantaneous phase — i.e. latch the display state at the readout tick. Alternatively raise the readout refresh to the frame rate. Either way, a screenshot must show one consistent instant.

findings.what: The room-in-plan pressure map is the loudest element in the frame (large saturated amber and cyan lobes, device x 255–765, y 195–780) and carries no colour key, no dB or Pa scale, and no axes. Nothing on screen says whether amber and cyan are opposite polarity or high and low magnitude, or what the contour spacing means. The label gives only 'pressure at 30.02 Hz, shown at 1 : 50 / right sub alone — Ψ₁₁₀ = −0.635'.
findings.fix: Add a two-swatch key inside the card ('+ / − pressure' or 'dB re. free field at 1 m') and label the contour interval, plus the sub and seat markers. If polarity is what the colours encode, say so — it is the whole reason the pair cancels the (1,1,0) mode. Also mark the room's W and D on the plan edges.

findings.what: shots/sub.png: the LEFT subwoofer's driver ring light blows to pure white in two places behind and below the plan card (device ≈ (395,845) and (390,700)), and the rack at x 60–260 is lit and competing. The plan card also sits on top of the left sub and the rack. Additionally the ROOM IN PLAN label wraps mid-number ('shown at 1 : / 50') and the 'Ψ₁₁₀ = 0 / the sofa sits on the centre line' label is struck through by the λ/2 dimension line.
findings.fix: Move the plan card right and up so it clears the left sub entirely, or push the left sub out of frame; reduce the ring-light emissive on the non-hero sub (or lower the bloom contribution of the meterGlow clone). Shorten the plan kicker to 'ROOM IN PLAN · 7.4 × 9 m · 1 : 50' so it does not wrap, and move the Ψ₁₁₀ label above the dimension line (offset [0, −22]).

findings.what: The label 'RETURN PATH · DF 400 → 130' (amp.js:890-893) states damping factor as a bald headline number, while the panel three inches away argues that DF is the misleading quantity and that the real change is 5.42 → 5.46 Ω, 0.76 %. A reader who reads only the picture takes away exactly the myth the piece is trying to kill. xover.js makes the same DF 130 → 7.5 claim in its .eq while its own prose says 'damping factor is the wrong quantity to quote'.
findings.fix: Change the amp label value to the quantity that means something: 'total damping R 5.42 → 5.46 Ω · +0.8 %' with the DF figures demoted to the kicker if at all. In xover.js:608, put the RD_ACT → RD_PAS pair in the .eq and move DF into the commentary span.

findings.what: The 'INSIDE THE CABLE' label prints 'ratio 7.8 × 10¹¹' immediately beside a drawing in which the field front crosses the 3 m run in 1.0 real second while the carriers oscillate with a 10.5 mm amplitude at 2 Hz — an as-drawn speed ratio of about 6 : 1. Both exaggerations are individually stated (CAR_EXAG ≈ 1.0×10⁶ spatial, FRONT_RAT ≈ 6.6×10⁷ temporal) and both are arithmetically correct against what is drawn, but they are of different kinds and the reader is never told the combined effect. power.js does state it ('as drawn only ×12 faster than the carriers, truly ×4.8×10¹¹'); amp, turntable and overview do not.
findings.fix: Add the as-drawn ratio to the label value in amp.js:894-898, to turntable.js's 'ONE LOOP, TWO SPEEDS' label, and to overview.js's MAINS · CLOSED LOOP / FIELD FRONT pair — computed, not asserted: (drawn front speed)/(drawn carrier peak speed). Use power.js:81-83 (SEEN_DRIFT / SEEN_FIELD / SEEN_RATIO) as the template.

findings.what: rms/peak confusion on one page. phono.js:24 declares V_REF = 0.05 m/s 'peak — the 5 cm/s reference' and uses it for the excursion arithmetic (a = v̂/ω = 7.96 µm, correct for 5 cm/s PEAK). phono.js:41 then declares V_CART = 0.30e-3 'V rms, MC open-circuit at 5 cm/s' and the .eq prints '0.300 mV — cartridge, 5 cm/s at 1 kHz'. If 5 cm/s is peak the output at that velocity is 0.30 mV PEAK = 0.212 mV rms, and the whole gain budget (V_IN, G_TOTAL 77.31 dB, SNR 68.8 dB) is 3 dB out. turntable.js gets this right — it derives 403 µV pk = 285 µV rms from 5 cm/s peak.
findings.fix: Adopt turntable.js's convention: V_CART = 285e-6 V rms at 5 cm/s peak (or state 'V rms at 5 cm/s rms' and change V_REF to 0.0707 m/s peak for the excursion side). Recompute LOAD_DB, V_IN, G_TOTAL, G_REST, SNR_DB and the .eq lines. This also removes the 285 vs 300 µV disagreement with the turntable chapter.

findings.what: The pinned readout 'ZOH 20 kHz −3.17 dB' is the non-oversampling figure, while the same chapter states the converter interpolates ×8 and holds at 352.8 kHz where the aperture costs −0.046 dB. The instrument cluster therefore reports a droop this converter does not have. Additionally all six DAC readouts are constants — the cluster shows nothing live on the one stage with the most animation.
findings.fix: Change the readout to 'ZOH 20 kHz' = ZOH_20K_OS (−0.046 dB) with u: 'dB · ×8 hold', or label it 'ZOH (NOS)'. Replace two of the six constants with live values from the animation — e.g. the current kernel count in the sinc build-up and the instantaneous reconstructed sample value.

findings.what: content() overruns the 320-word cap (ADDENDUM §C) on eight of twelve stages, measured from the rendered DOM with .eq blocks excluded: amp 428, power 400, streamer 385, air 359, xover 357, phono 347, turntable 343, preamp 338. sub 321 is borderline. Only overview (293), speaker (291) and dac (314) comply. In every one of these the prose scrolls out of sight below the pinned readouts.
findings.fix: Cut to 320. amp: drop the Damping section entirely (it duplicates the xover argument) and compress the Heat paragraph. power: cut the Fermi-velocity/mean-free-path sentence to one clause. streamer: cut the buffer/master-clock paragraph. air: cut the reverberant-field paragraph to one sentence. xover: cut the passive-network paragraph to the .eq plus one sentence.

findings.what: src/stages/speaker.js:757 and 1017 draw the live excursion dimension centred on x = 0, while the Xmax gate hairlines (lines 761-767) are centred on X_GAPC = −0.02425 (the coil's axial centre). The two rulers sit side by side at the same height with centres 24 mm apart in section-local units (~74 px on screen), so the reader compares live travel against an Xmax scale that is offset from it. The comparison is the whole point of the pair.
findings.fix: Change dm[0].write and dm[1]/dm[2].position.x in update() to be centred on X_GAPC: [X_GAPC ± xp, −0.094, 0.006], and likewise the static dim built at line 757.

findings.what: The '45/45 GROOVE — 1800 : 1 · MOTION 1 : 1000' label's value line is truncated on screen: it reads 'tip 18 µm across × 5 µm along · pitch 12' and stops mid-number (the full string is 'pitch 129 µm'). The label box is clipped by its own max-width, cut off by the neighbouring 'MOVING COIL' label at device x ≈ 745.
findings.fix: Shorten the value to 'tip 18 × 5 µm · pitch 129 µm' and move the MOVING COIL label right or down so the two boxes do not abut. Verify by reading the rendered .wlab bounding rects for overlap.

findings.what: The 'OCXO · 5.6448 MHz = 128 f_s · the whole jitter budget is 0.77 ps rms' label is anchored at device (485,797), which in shots/streamer.png is over the POWER CONDITIONER in bay 0, not over the streamer in bay 1 or its clock island. The label makes a specific claim about a specific part and points at the wrong chassis.
findings.fix: Re-anchor to the clock island (the code comments place it 60 mm behind the fascia, streamer.js:120) with a short leader, and give it offset that keeps the box over the streamer's own chassis.

findings.what: streamer.js:52 RETX_ONE_IN = 380 is an invented constant, but content() states it as fact: 'one in 380 has to be sent again'. Same for BUF_TARGET = 120 ms and STALL_MEAN = 0.090 s — the buffer figure is at least flagged as 'a wired-LAN figure' in a code comment the reader never sees. Contract §6 requires every number on screen to be derived from stated inputs or an explicitly stated premise.
findings.fix: Write it as a stated modelling premise in the prose: 'modelled here at one segment in 380 needing a retransmission, with a 4.5 ms fast-retransmit round trip' and 'a 120 ms target buffer, a wired-LAN figure'.

findings.what: The label 'AES3 SUBFRAME · CELLS AT 1 : 117,600' derives CELL_RATIO from BCLK = 64 fs = 2.8224 MHz (streamer.js:46), but the content() prose correctly says biphase-mark coding puts TWO half-cells in every bit, so the line's cell rate is 128 fs = 5.6448 MHz. If what is drawn are biphase cells the ratio is 235,200 : 1, not 117,600 : 1; if what is drawn are bits the label should say 'bits', not 'cells'.
findings.fix: Decide which the drawn elements are. If half-cells, use MCLK: CELL_RATIO = Math.round(MCLK / CELL_PER_REAL_S) = 235,200 and keep the word 'cells'. If bits, change the kicker to 'BITS AT 1 : 117,600'.

findings.what: The 'AT THE SEAT' label prints '91.4 dB/2.83 V/1 m · 100 W peak' and then '110.3 dB at 1 m'. A reader doing the obvious sum gets 91.4 + 10·log10(100) = 111.4 dB. The 1.1 dB difference is because 91.4 dB is referred to 2.83 V (= 1.29 W into 6.2 Ω) while the 100 W is real watts — content() explains this but the label does not, so the label's three numbers do not close.
findings.fix: Change the label text line to '90.3 dB/1 W/1 m · 100 W peak' (SENS_1W, which the 110.3 dB figure actually follows from) and leave the 91.4 dB/2.83 V figure to the panel.

findings.what: content() says the passive network costs '11.7 % of the power burnt in copper before the cone'. LOSS_PCT (line 63) is computed from RS_PAS = 1.0614 Ω, which includes the 41.4 mΩ of speaker cable and the 20 mΩ amplifier output impedance — both present in the active case too. The network's own share is 1.00/9.06 = 11.0 %. The sentence also sits immediately beside '−1.02 dB against the active case', which corresponds to 20.8 % less power delivered; two different loss fractions read as one.
findings.fix: Compute LOSS_PCT from R_NET alone (11.0 %) and say 'burnt in the network's copper'. Separate the two sentences so the −1.02 dB insertion loss and the 11.0 % network dissipation are not read as the same quantity.

findings.what: content() refers to 'the shaded decades are where the groove stops getting wider', but the shading (phono.js:452) is drawn at flatMat(PAL.am, 0.013) — 1.3 % opacity. In the render it is a barely-perceptible tint with no boundary marks or caption, so the prose points at something the reader effectively cannot see. Separately, the green 'record + playback = 0.00 dB' trace is flat by construction (riaaRecordDb is defined as −riaaPlaybackDb), so the graph demonstrates a tautology rather than a result.
findings.fix: Raise the band opacity to ~0.06 and add a one-word caption at the top of each band ('constant amplitude'). For the sum, either say plainly in the prose that the two curves are one function and its algebraic inverse so the sum is exact by definition and the only real error is tolerance (±0.10 dB, already computed), or build the record curve from an independent pole/zero network so the cancellation is demonstrated rather than assumed.

findings.what: content() states 'Cyan is the reconstruction; red the hold and the sub-thermal region'. CONTRACT §3.5 reserves red for marking a myth. Using it for the zero-order hold — which the same page is at pains to say is a legitimate intermediate, not the myth — and for the sub-thermal amplitude band inverts the piece's own colour language.
findings.fix: Draw the ZOH staircase in amber (energy/intermediate) and the sub-thermal band in a dim neutral; keep red for the staircase-as-myth callout only, if it appears at all.

findings.what: Dead instrument clusters. All six DAC readouts are compile-time constants (FS, WORD, NYQUIST, LSB, SNR 24-BIT, ZOH). Four of six streamer readouts are constants (PAYLOAD, BIT CLOCK, JITTER, SNR 10 kHz). xover has two (CROSSOVER, SLOPE), sub has three (MODE, DRIVE, SCHROEDER), speaker's SPL @ 1 m never moves because it is the drive premise, turntable's PLATTER and CONTACT P never move. The footer is described in the addendum as 'the instrument cluster'; a cluster where two thirds of the dials are painted on is not one.
findings.fix: Cap constants at two per stage and give the rest live values. DAC: current kernel count, instantaneous reconstructed voltage, live in-band noise at the cursor, ZOH droop at the cursor frequency. streamer: live buffer occupancy (already there), live arrival rate (already there), live Δt and its dBFS error from the eye. sub: live seat SPL as the second sub fades in, live Ψ sum.

findings.what: The cabinets do not read as the described Wilson-idiom faceted gloss floorstander. In both shots/speaker.png and shots/overview.png they render as plain light-grey rectangular boxes with a visibly detached head module — the rake (3.5° / 11°), the gloss lacquer on the flanks and the alloy gantry are not legible, and the pianoBlack body reads mid-grey rather than black. In the overview the loudspeakers are the least convincing objects in the room.
findings.fix: Check that mats().pianoBlack survives speaker.js's hw() clone with its clearcoat intact, raise its envMapIntensity so the gloss picks up the front wraps, and increase the visual separation between head and bass modules by making the alloy gantry brighter and slightly proud. Then re-shoot overview and confirm the cabinets read as one object, not three stacked boxes.

findings.what: The planar floor reflection returns the rack, both monoblocks and the cabling at close to the brightness of the real objects (shots/overview.png, y 850–1100), so the scene reads as standing in water and the reflected rack competes with the real one for the eye. The same over-bright reflection doubles the subwoofers in shots/sub.png and the rack in shots/preamp.png.
findings.fix: This is a core reflector setting, so report rather than patch: the planar reflection needs a stronger distance falloff and a lower base intensity (roughly half). If it must be fixed per stage, place a low-opacity dark plane over the reflection zone behind the hero.

findings.what: src/core/dsp.js:196-201, classABDissipation: the comment says 'Total device dissipation, both halves: P_d = Vcc²/(π²·RL) at m = 2/π'. The function is correct but the total at m = 2/π is 2·Vcc²/(π²·RL) — the quoted expression is the per-half figure. Not displayed anywhere, but amp.js reimplements this and a future author reading the comment would be off by 2×.
findings.fix: Correct the comment to 'P_d(total) = 2·Vcc²/(π²·RL) at m = 2/π, i.e. Vcc²/(π²·RL) per half'. Core is frozen, so report only.

findings.what: src/stages/turntable.js:38 comment states the Baerwald relation as 'r1·r2 = 2LD − D²'. The code (line 42) correctly uses K = L² − D² via OVERHANG = L − √(L² − r1r2). 2LD − D² = L² − OH², which is a different quantity. The arithmetic on screen (17.32 mm overhang, 221.68 mm mounting distance, 23.02° offset) is right; only the comment is wrong.
findings.fix: Change the comment to 'r1·r2 = L² − D²'.

findings.what: The 'THE FIRST TWO AT TRUE ×26 · THE THIRD THAT SAME SWING ×1000 MORE' comparison row at Y_DIM = 0.400 is a good idea executed at zero legibility. At ×26 the true 1.31 µm swing is 34 µm of card, which is about 0.04 device pixels — the middle term of a three-term comparison is literally invisible. The row sits crammed against the card's top border with the conductor-diameter mark and the blown-up mark 150 px apart and nothing between them.
findings.fix: Draw the true-swing term as an explicit zero-width tick with its own caption ('at this scale, ±1.31 µm is 0.04 px — this mark') so the invisibility is the point rather than an omission, and move the whole row down inside the card with 20 px of clearance from the plate edge.

findings.what: The 'LADDER AFTER THE GAIN BLOCK' and 'LATE LADDER − EARLY LADDER +9.57 dB' labels are printed on top of the S/N traces (device (455,690) and (330,775) in shots/preamp.png) with no leader to the green gap marker they describe, and the relay-ladder board drawing carries no indication of which block is the 32 dB section and which the 1 dB — the '010111' bit string cannot be mapped to the picture.
findings.fix: Move both labels clear of the plot area (above the graph, offset [0,−20] and [0,−20] from the top-left and top-right corners) and add small '32 16 8 4 2 1' numerals under the six relay blocks on the board so the bit string reads against the drawing.

findings.what: The crossover chassis occupies roughly 145 px of a 1250-px frame and the preamp directly below it (with the bright '−32' display and two blown-out knobs) is larger and brighter, so the eye goes to the wrong box. The chassis's two frequency-select knobs also blow to pure white. The card and its labels are otherwise the best in the piece.
findings.fix: Reframe on the chassis half-height (radius ~0.05 rather than 0.27) with fill ~0.34 so the crossover is 280–350 px tall and shrink the card proportionally; reduce the knob material's envMapIntensity or roughness so the chrome marks do not clip.

findings.what: The whole frame is a soft grey haze: a large diffuse wash covers device x 500–1450, y 200–750, and every object (rack, speakers, subs, turntable) is desaturated and low-contrast behind it. The parcel card at the bottom-left has a stray grey diagonal bar crossing it at x 350–410, and the AIR PARCELS label sits 220 px above the card it describes with no leader.
findings.fix: Identify and cut the wash (most likely an oversized additive sprite or a fog volume in air.js's build). Move the AIR PARCELS label to the card's top edge with occlude:false, and check what the diagonal bar at the card's left is — it should not cross the parcel grid.
